cross_cutting_finding.headline: The S107 thin-tape guard is LOAD-BEARING on this block on its very first ride, and it fires in the direction that DISARMS a signal, not one that creates one. finding_1_thin_tape_guard.claim: flow.big_print_bshare_thin_tape_guard changes the answer on 20260528, and it changes it by REMOVING the only fire in the accumulation window. Session 20260525 (Memorial Day, thin) carries big_print_b_share 0.599 on big_prints_n = 13. Under a fixed 0.55 bar that clears and is the single fire in the >= 2-of-~5 window that structure.accumulation_arm_turn needs. Under the guard (n <= ~20 -> bar 0.60) it does NOT clear - 0.599 misses by one thousandth. The full window for 20260528 is 0522 0.503 (n=140), 0525 0.599 (n=13, DISARMED), 0526 0.425 (n=81), 0527 0.529 (n=196): ZERO clean fires, so the accumulation arm correctly does NOT fire and I did not use it. This is exactly the over-fire-on-noise the play predicts (q1 median 9 big prints, sd 0.255 = double the other quartiles), and it lands on a holiday session, which is the class most likely to produce a spurious thin-tape extreme. RECOMMENDED as forward evidence for the play's PROPOSAL status: first prospective fire, and it fired as a SUPPRESSOR.
finding_1_thin_tape_guard.generality: This is a general mechanism, not a G20 fact: holiday-thinned sessions systematically enter the >= 2-of-~5 accumulation window and systematically carry the thinnest big-print samples. Any block containing a market holiday will have its accumulation/conviction arms distorted by exactly one session unless the guard is applied. That is a structural interaction between the calendar and a proportion-based signal, and it will recur on every holiday block.
